title: One Borrow Step
statement: Let $B$ and $F$ be Boolean finite Turing machines, let $a$ be a state of $B$, and choose Boolean parameters `forward` and `findMode`, an input word $x$, a base configuration of the loop host on $x$, an input-head position $p$, and Boolean words $u$ and $v$. From controller phase $8$, with flag and payload tapes blank, counter tape storing $uv$, counter head at $|u|$, payload head at $0$, and empty output, one step leads to the following configuration: if $v$ is empty, phase $10$ with counter storing $u$ and head at $|u|-1$; if $v$ begins with true, phase $9$ with counter storing $u\,\mathrm{false}\,v'$ and head at $|u|-1$; and if $v$ begins with false, phase $8$ with counter storing $u\,\mathrm{true}\,v'$ and head at $|u|+1$, where $v'$ is the remaining suffix. In each case the other frame data are unchanged, the flag and payload tapes remain blank, and the output remains empty.
hypotheses_covered: initial flag and payload tapes are blank
replaced:
Let $p$ and $r$ be Boolean words. One step of the loop host from its borrow phase on a
frame whose counter track is the buffer tape of $p$ followed by $r$ with counter head at
$|p|$ behaves as the standalone decrement machine: an empty $r$ enters the underflow-
rewind phase moving left; a leading $\mathrm{true}$ writes $\mathrm{false}$ and enters
the success-rewind phase moving left; a leading $\mathrm{false}$ writes $\mathrm{true}$
and continues the borrow moving right. Only the counter track changes.
